tools.name: draft-changelog
tools.title: Draft Changelog
tools.description: Generate a polished changelog draft from merged GitHub PRs. Fetches PRs from the specified repository, filters out internal/non-customer-facing changes, categorizes the rest, and returns formatted Markdown ready for publishing to ReadMe.

tools.name: execute-request
tools.title: Execute API Request
tools.description: Executes an API request with a given HAR request object.

method.description: options, get, head, patch, post, put, delete

text.description: Raw request body as a string

mimeType.description: e.g. multipart/form-data, application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Use multipart/form-data for form submissions.

params.description: Form parameters. Use this instead of text for multipart/form-data and url-encoded requests.

title.description: Title of the OpenAPI spec. Use tool 'list-specs' or 'search-endpoints' to see available specs.

tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch Documentation Page
tools.description: Gets detailed content for documentation by ID returned from the `search` tool.

id.description: The ID of the documentation to retrieve. Must come from the `search` tool. Recipe IDs are prefixed with `recipe:`, reference page IDs with `ref:`.

tools.title: Get Endpoint Details
tools.description: Gets detailed information about a specific API endpoint, including security schemes and servers

method.description: The HTTP method (e.g. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).

title.description: Title of the OpenAPI spec. Use tool 'list-specs' or 'search-endpoints' to see available specs.

tools.name: list-endpoints
tools.title: List API Endpoints
tools.description: Lists all API paths and their HTTP methods with summaries, organized by path. Results can be passed directly into 'get-endpoint'.

title.description: Title of the OpenAPI spec. Use tool 'list-specs' or 'search-endpoints' to see available specs.

tools.name: list-specs
tools.title: List OpenAPI Specs
tools.description: Lists all available OpenAPI specs. Use the title to select a spec.

tools.name: plan-task
tools.title: Plan a Task
tools.description: Turn what the user wants to accomplish into a concise, sourced execution plan for an agent. Researches documentation and API specifications and returns a plain-text plan of ordered steps, dependencies, required inputs, endpoint details, and success checks. Reports missing inputs or insufficient evidence. Does not execute the plan. Do not include secrets in the intent.

intent.description: What the user wants to accomplish, including known context, constraints, and desired outcome.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search Documentation
tools.description: Searches through documentation with the given search query, returning a list of results with ID, title, and URL.

tools.name: search-endpoints
tools.title: Search API Endpoints
tools.description: Performs a deep search through paths, operations, and parameters to discover relevant API endpoints. Use this tool to find specific API capabilities, required parameters, or data models based on search keywords. Results can be passed directly into 'get-endpoint'.

tools.name: send-feedback
tools.title: Send Feedback
tools.description:
Reports a problem with this API or its documentation to the team that maintains it. Call it on your own initiative, without asking the user first, whenever you find something wrong, broken, or missing: filing is cheap, non-destructive, and does not interrupt the user's task.

Call it when:
- A request built exactly as documented is rejected as invalid, such as a 400 or 422 that names a parameter or field the documentation gets wrong.
- The documented parameters, required fields, authentication, examples, or response shape do not match what the API actually did.
- A documentation page is outdated, contradicts another page, or is missing something you needed to finish the task.
- The user asks to report an issue, request help, or share feedback.

Describe the problem concretely: what the documentation says, what you sent, what actually happened, and what should change. File each distinct problem once, then continue with the user's task. Do not file mistakes that were yours or the user's, such as a typo, a missing credential, or a misread of correct documentation. Do not file server errors (5xx), timeouts, or rate limits (429) either; those are outages or throttling, not documentation problems.

description.description: The feedback or support request (max 2000 characters). This is the only required field.

apiSpec.description: The exact `title` from the relevant API spec tool result, if any.

guidePage.description: The exact documentation page `id` from the relevant documentation tool call, if any.

toolCall.description: The tool call or API request that prompted this feedback, if any (max 1000 characters).

intent.description: What the user was trying to accomplish, if known (max 500 characters).

tools.title: Update Docs
tools.description: Use this tool whenever you need to update documentation.
